user_text: Plan a 1-day migration from SVN to Git for a small repo.
assistant_text:
# 1-Day SVN to Git Migration Plan

## Pre-Migration Checklist (Night Before)

- [ ] Notify all team members — **freeze SVN commits** during migration
- [ ] Confirm Git hosting destination (GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, self-hosted)
- [ ] Ensure you have admin access to both SVN and Git servers
- [ ] Back up the SVN repository

```bash
# Backup SVN repo
svnadmin dump /path/to/svn/repo > svn_backup.dump
```

---

## Morning: Preparation (2–3 hours)

### Step 1 — Install Tools
```bash
# macOS
brew install git git-svn svn

# Ubuntu/Debian
sudo apt install git git-svn subversion

# Verify
git svn --version
```

### Step 2 — Map SVN Authors to Git Authors
SVN uses usernames; Git needs `Name <email>` format.

```bash
# Extract all SVN authors
svn log --quiet svn://your-repo-url | \
  grep "^r" | \
  awk '{print $3}' | \
  sort -u > authors.txt
```

Create `authors-transform.txt`:
```
jsmith = John Smith <john.smith@company.com>
mjones = Mary Jones <mary.jones@company.com>
deploy = Deploy Bot <deploy@company.com>
```

### Step 3 — Identify Your SVN Layout
```
Standard layout?          Non-standard layout?
├── trunk/                ├── code/
├── branches/             ├── releases/
└── tags/                 └── experiments/
```

---

## Late Morning: The Migration (2–3 hours)

### Step 4 — Clone SVN Repo with git-svn

**Standard trunk/branches/tags layout:**
```bash
git svn clone svn://your-repo-url \
  --stdlayout \
  --authors-file=authors-transform.txt \
  --no-metadata \
  -A authors-transform.txt \
  my-project-git

cd my-project-git
```

**Non-standard layout:**
```bash
git svn clone svn://your-repo-url \
  --trunk=code \
  --branches=releases \
  --tags=experiments \
  --authors-file=authors-transform.txt \
  --no-metadata \
  my-project-git
```

> ⏱️ **Large repos can take 1–4 hours.** Run in a `screen` or `tmux` session.

### Step 5 — Convert SVN Branches & Tags
```bash
# Convert remote SVN branches to local Git branches
for branch in $(git branch -r | grep -v "tags/" | grep -v trunk); do
  git branch "${branch##*/}" "$branch"
done

# Convert SVN tags to proper Git tags
for tag in $(git branch -r | grep "tags/"); do
  git tag "${tag##*/tags/}" "$tag"
  git branch -d -r "$tag"
done

# Clean up remote tracking refs
git for-each-ref refs/remotes | \
  cut -d/ -f3- | \
  grep -v HEAD | \
  while read ref; do git branch -d -r "$ref"; done
```

---

## Early Afternoon: Cleanup & Validation (1–2 hours)

### Step 6 — Clean Up the Repo
```bash
# Remove SVN tracking files
find . -name ".svn" -type d -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null

# Add a .gitignore if missing
curl -o .gitignore https://www.toptal.com/developers/gitignore/api/svn

# Run garbage collection
git gc --aggressive --prune=now
```

### Step 7 — Validate History
```bash
# Check commit count matches SVN
git log --oneline | wc -l

# Verify authors were mapped correctly
git log --format="%an <%ae>" | sort -u

# Check branches and tags
git branch -a
git tag -l

# Spot-check a few commits
git log --oneline -20
git show HEAD
```

---

## Afternoon: Push & Finalize (1–2 hours)

### Step 8 — Push to Remote Git Host
```bash
# Add your new remote
git remote add origin https://github.com/your-org/my-project.git

# Push all branches
git push origin --all

# Push all tags
git push origin --tags

# Verify on the hosting platform
```

### Step 9 — Update Team Workflows

Send this to your team:

```bash
# Each developer runs:
git clone https://github.com/your-org/my-project.git
cd my-project

# Set up identity (if not global)
git config user.name "Your Name"
git config user.email "you@company.com"
```

### Step 10 — Lock Down SVN
```bash
# Add a pre-commit hook to SVN to block new commits
cat > /path/to/svn/repo/hooks/pre-commit << 'EOF'
#!/bin/sh
echo "This repository has been migrated to Git."
echo "New location: https://github.com/your-org/my-project"
exit 1
EOF
chmod +x /path/to/svn/repo/hooks/pre-commit
```

---

## End of Day: Verification Checklist

| Check | Status |
|---|---|
| All commits migrated | ☐ |
| Authors correctly mapped | ☐ |
| Branches present in Git | ☐ |
| Tags present in Git | ☐ |
| CI/CD pipelines updated | ☐ |
| Team notified with new URL | ☐ |
| SVN write access disabled | ☐ |
| README updated with Git workflow | ☐ |

---

## Troubleshooting Quick Reference

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| Unknown author error | Add missing user to `authors-transform.txt`, re-run |
| Clone hangs/times out | Use `--revision HEAD:1` to clone in reverse, or clone in chunks |
| Tags show as branches | Re-run Step 5 tag conversion |
| Binary files corrupted | Check SVN `svn:mime-type` properties before migration |
| History looks wrong | Compare `svn log` count vs `git log` count |

---

## Timeline Summary

| Time | Task |
|---|---|
| 08:00 | Install tools, extract authors, freeze SVN |
| 09:00 | Build author map, identify layout |
| 10:00 | Start `git svn clone` |
| 12:00 | Lunch — clone running in background |
| 13:00 | Convert branches/tags, clean up |
| 14:00 | Validate history |
| 15:00 | Push to remote, update CI/CD |
| 16:00 | Notify team, disable SVN writes |
| 17:00 | Done ✅ |

> **Tip:** For repos with 10,000+ revisions, consider doing the clone overnight and starting the plan at Step 5.

Based on the migration plan above, the top 3 risks are:

---

## Top 3 Risks

### 1. 🧑‍💻 Incomplete Author Mapping
**What goes wrong:** Any SVN username missing from `authors-transform.txt` causes `git svn clone` to **abort mid-migration**, forcing a restart from scratch.

**Impact:** Hours of lost clone time, delayed migration.

**Mitigation:**
```bash
# Double-check no authors are missing BEFORE cloning
svn log --quiet svn://your-repo-url | grep "^r" | \
  awk '{print $3}' | sort -u
# Cross-reference every name against your authors file
```

---

### 2. ⏱️ Clone Takes Longer Than Expected
**What goes wrong:** Large or old repos with thousands of revisions can take **far longer than anticipated**, blowing past your 1-day window — especially on slow network connections to a remote SVN server.

**Impact:** Migration bleeds into the next day while SVN remains frozen and the team is blocked.

**Mitigation:**
- Run a **test clone** of the last 100 revisions the night before to estimate speed
- Always run inside `screen` or `tmux`
- Have a fallback plan — agreed extra freeze window with the team

```bash
# Test clone speed with a small slice first
git svn clone svn://your-repo-url --revision HEAD:$(( HEAD - 100 )) ...
```

---

### 3. 🔀 Developers Committing to SVN During Migration
**What goes wrong:** Someone doesn't see the freeze notice and pushes to SVN **after your clone started**, meaning those commits are missing from Git on day one.

**Impact:** Lost work, or an emergency re-migration after go-live.

**Mitigation:**
- Apply the SVN `pre-commit` hook **before** starting the clone, not after
- Send freeze notice via **multiple channels** (email, Slack, in-person)
- Do a final `svn log -r HEAD` check immediately before pushing to Git to confirm no new revisions appeared

---

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Biggest Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Incomplete author map | High | Medium | Pre-extract & verify authors the night before |
| Clone timeout | Medium | High | Test clone speed early; have extra time buffer |
| Commits during freeze | Low | High | Lock SVN writes before clone starts |

## Pre-Migration Checklist

- [ ] Back up the SVN repository
- [ ] Freeze SVN commits and notify the team
- [ ] Extract and verify **all** SVN authors are mapped
- [ ] Test clone speed with a small revision slice
- [ ] Run clone inside `screen` or `tmux`
- [ ] Lock SVN with a `pre-commit` hook before cloning
- [ ] Validate commit count and authors after clone
- [ ] Push all branches and tags to Git
- [ ] Confirm CI/CD pipelines point to new repo
- [ ] Notify team of new Git URL

## Rollback Option

**Keep SVN as-is and revert the pre-commit hook.**

If the migration fails, remove the blocking hook to restore SVN write access:

```bash
rm /path/to/svn/repo/hooks/pre-commit
```

The original SVN repository remains untouched throughout the migration — `git svn clone` only **reads** from it, so no SVN data is ever modified or lost. The team can resume committing to SVN immediately while you diagnose and retry the migration.

> **Key assumption:** Do not decommission or delete the SVN server until the Git migration has been fully verified and the team has signed off.

## Prerequisite

**`git-svn` must be installed on the machine running the migration.**

Without it, the core `git svn clone` command will fail and the migration cannot proceed.

```bash
# Verify it is installed
git svn --version
```

user_text: What is the fastest validation step?
assistant_text:
## Fastest Validation Step

**Compare commit counts between SVN and Git.**

```bash
# SVN commit count
svn log svn://your-repo-url --quiet | grep "^r" | wc -l

# Git commit count
git log --oneline | wc -l
```

The two numbers should match. Takes **under 30 seconds** and immediately tells you whether history was fully migrated before you do anything else.
**08:00** Freeze SVN → **09:00** Build author map → **10:00** Clone → **13:00** Convert branches/tags → **14:00** Validate → **15:00** Push to Git → **16:00** Lock SVN → **17:00** Done ✅

user_text: Provide two tools you might use.
assistant_text:
## Two Tools

1. **`git-svn`** — migrates SVN history, branches, and tags directly into a Git repository via `git svn clone`.

2. **`svnadmin`** — backs up the SVN repository before migration via `svnadmin dump`, providing a safe restore point if anything goes wrong.

user_text: State who should approve the final cutover.
assistant_text:
## Final Cutover Approval

**The project or team lead** should approve the final cutover, as they are accountable for:

- Confirming the **team has been notified** and is no longer committing to SVN
- Signing off that **history and branches look correct** in Git
- Accepting responsibility if a **rollback is needed**

> No one should push to Git or lock SVN writes permanently until this person has given explicit go-ahead.

## Communication Tip

**Send the freeze notice and new Git URL in a single message** — combining both means the team knows exactly when to stop and where to go next, with no follow-up questions.

## Final Recap

| # | Step | Key Point |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Backup | `svnadmin dump` before anything else |
| 2 | Freeze SVN | Notify team via multiple channels |
| 3 | Map authors | Verify all usernames before cloning |
| 4 | Clone | Run `git svn clone` inside `tmux` or `screen` |
| 5 | Convert | Branches and tags need manual conversion |
| 6 | Validate | Match commit counts in SVN and Git |
| 7 | Push | Push all branches and tags to remote |
| 8 | Lock SVN | Apply `pre-commit` hook to block writes |
| 9 | Notify | Send new Git URL to the whole team |
| 10 | Sign off | Team lead approves final cutover |

**Top 3 risks:** Incomplete author map · Clone timeout · Commits during freeze

**Rollback:** Remove the `pre-commit` hook — SVN is untouched and ready to resume instantly

**One day. One repo. One clean migration.** ✅

- Back up SVN first
- Freeze commits early
- Map all authors before cloning
- Clone inside `tmux` or `screen`
- Convert branches and tags manually
- Match commit counts to validate
- Push all branches and tags to Git
- Lock SVN with a `pre-commit` hook
- Team lead approves final cutover
- Send new Git URL to the whole team ✅
